capabilities: open the active note in an external editor
open the vault folder in an external editor
detect or manually configure the editor executable path
reuse an already open editor window
test and debug the launch configuration
disambiguation: Not limited to VS Code despite the name; the editor executable can be overridden to launch Cursor, Trae, Zed or Windsurf.
extras: README addresses community-review permission flags for child_process and fs/path use, includes troubleshooting (exit code 9009, PATH inheritance, .zshrc on macOS) and documents the plugin bilingually in English and Simplified Chinese.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to hand the current note or the vault folder to an external code editor, and launching one from Electron often fails on Windows because PATHEXT is missing.

relations.evidence: Open the current Obsidian note in VS Code with one command: open the active file, or open the whole vault as a folder.
The editor executable can be overridden, so cursor, trae, zed and windsurf work too

requires.name: VS Code or another editor with a CLI (Cursor, Trae, Zed, Windsurf)

summary: Command that opens the current note or the vault folder in VS Code or a configurable editor such as Cursor, Zed, Trae or Windsurf.
